summary: Describes standard programming interfaces for the Service Location Protocol in C and Java, so applications can discover services in a consistent way. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A toolbox of ready-made buttons that programmers can press to ask the network where services are, with one version for each of two languages.

subtitle: Standard C and Java programming interfaces, plus file formats, for finding network services with the Service Location Protocol.

tldr.problem: Programs that want to find or advertise network services with the Service Location Protocol (SLP) would otherwise need code specific to each SLP implementation.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines C and Java bindings, a configuration file format and a serialized registration file format, so source code and settings work across implementations.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational document. Applications written to the API are meant to be source portable between SLP implementations.

today: RFC 2614 is an Informational RFC and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it. It builds on the protocol in RFC 2608.

sections.title: Goals and Vocabulary
sections.content:
The Service Location API gives standard access to the Service Location Protocol (SLP), which is specified in RFC 2608. Bindings are defined for C and Java. The main goal is source portability of applications between SLP implementations, which should make it easier to adopt SLP.

The C binding aims for minimal but complete access with simple memory management and small code size. The Java API aims for modular implementations and an object oriented interface. The RFC uses three kinds of agent: a User Agent (UA) makes requests for clients, a Service Agent (SA) advertises services, and a Directory Agent (DA) gathers advertisements from SAs to hand to UAs. Scopes are strings that group services, mainly for scalability.
sections.eli5: Some programs want to find helpers on the network, and others want to say "I am here." This document says how both kinds of programs talk to the finding service in the same way.

sections.title: Configuration and Registration Files
sections.content:
Two file formats are defined, both in UTF-8 and both with an ABNF grammar. The configuration file is a list of property=value lines that set SLP and network parameters. Examples include net.slp.useScopes, net.slp.DAAddresses, net.slp.multicastTTL (default 255) and net.slp.MTU (default 1400 bytes). Most properties can be changed at run time through the API, but net.slp.useScopes, net.slp.DAAddresses and net.slp.isBroadcastOnly are read-only.

The serialized registration file lists registrations that a DA or SA server loads at start-up. It exists mainly for older service programs that cannot be converted to SLP, and for exchanging registrations between implementations. A lifetime of 65535 seconds marks a registration as permanent.

If a file has a format error, the agent logs it, uses the default for the bad property and carries on. An agent MUST NOT fail because of it.
sections.eli5: One sheet is a list of settings, like how loud to shout. The other is a guest list of services that should be announced even if they cannot announce themselves.

sections.title: Rules Shared by Both Bindings
sections.content:
Implementations must make API calls thread-safe. Registrations carry a lifetime, and the SA API must offer automatic refreshing, though a client using it should deregister explicitly before it exits. A UA SHOULD remove duplicate results in synchronous operation, but may skip that during asynchronous C use to save memory. No string parameter may exceed 64K bytes.

For errors, a synchronous call reports an error only if no successful reply arrived from any SLP entity. Error names are consistent between the C and Java APIs, for example SCOPE_NOT_SUPPORTED, NETWORK_TIMED_OUT, PARAMETER_BAD and NOT_IMPLEMENTED. A subset implementation must still provide every interface and return NOT_IMPLEMENTED for what it lacks.

Scope discovery follows a fixed priority. Scopes configured by DHCP come first, then the net.slp.useScopes property, then the scopes of configured DAs. Failing all of those, an SA uses the scope DEFAULT, and a UA uses active and passive DA discovery or SA discovery. The API must always return some scope.
sections.eli5: Both versions follow the same house rules: be safe when many things happen at once, tell the program clearly when something goes wrong, and always have a place to look.

sections.title: The C Binding
sections.content:
The C binding is a thin layer over the protocol, with one function per protocol request. SLPOpen() returns an SLPHandle for a language locale and says whether the handle is synchronous or asynchronous. The main calls are SLPReg(), SLPDereg(), SLPDelAttrs(), SLPFindSrvTypes(), SLPFindSrvs() and SLPFindAttrs(). Helpers include SLPFindScopes(), SLPParseSrvURL(), SLPEscape(), SLPUnescape() and SLPFree().

Results come back through callbacks that carry an error code and a client-supplied cookie. The callback memory belongs to the library, so the client MUST copy anything it wants to keep. A handle can run one operation at a time, and a callback must not call back into the API on the same handle, or it gets SLP_HANDLE_IN_USE. The last callback receives SLP_LAST_CALL.

Setting the lifetime in SLPReg() to SLP_LIFETIME_MAXIMUM (65535) asks the library to refresh the URL automatically. SLP_LIFETIME_DEFAULT is 10800 seconds, which is 3 hours.
sections.eli5: In the C version you open a line, say what you want, and the library calls you back each time it hears an answer. You must write the answer down yourself, because the library takes its paper back.

sections.title: The Java Binding
sections.content:
The Java API models SLP as classes and interfaces in a single package. ServiceLocationManager hands out a Locator, which gives UA ability, and an Advertiser, which gives SA ability. TemplateRegistry supports service template introspection and attribute type checking. ServiceURL, ServiceType and ServiceLocationAttribute model the basic SLP concepts.

All errors come through one exception class, ServiceLocationException, with an integer error code, because many exception subclasses would cost code size. Bad arguments raise IllegalArgumentException. The Java API has no special asynchronous support: results come as a ServiceLocationEnumeration, which an implementation can fill as answers arrive. Unlike C, the Java API must collate returned attribute values.

The design allows modular implementations that provide only SA, only UA, or only template access, by returning null from the creation method.
sections.eli5: In the Java version you ask a manager for a finder or an announcer tool, then use it like any other object. If a toolbox leaves out a tool, the manager says so.

sections.title: Internationalization and Security
sections.content:
Security is handled inside the API library and is shown to clients only as exceptions. The net.slp.securityEnabled property (default false) controls whether an SA signs its messages, but a UA must be ready for an authentication exception at any time.

Without SLP message authentication, an adversary could delete valid advertisements, supply false service information and hide existing services. The RFC says all SLP agents should be configured to use SLP SPIs. For language, every request and registration is tagged with a locale, and the dialect part of the tag is matched on a best effort basis.
sections.eli5: Without a secret handshake, a trickster could remove real signs or put up fake ones. The library does the handshake for you and only tells you if it fails.

items.title: User Agent
items.text: Makes SLP requests for a client, going to DAs when they exist.

items.title: Service Agent
items.text: Lets service software register and deregister, and answers UA requests.

items.title: Directory Agent
items.text: Collects advertisements from SAs to provide to UAs.
